We develop a stablecoin-specific threat model, map cryptographic dependencies to monetary control surfaces, and classify migration choices along three dimensions: who can authorize a change, where the change must occur, and whether it is hybrid, post-quantum native, or an encapsulation of a classical component. We emphasize an authority-liability gap: the party able to migrate a component is often different from the holders, exchanges, protocols, or issuers that bear the loss if it fails. We review the relevant cryptographic primitives, but distinguish general blockchain failures from their stablecoin-specific effects. We also examine recent blockchain and issuer-controlled interoperability proposals, and relate migration choices to redemption, continuity, and intervention requirements under current stablecoin regulation. Our findings identify open problems in aggregate and threshold authorization, operation-specific security levels and costs, dormant and wrapped supply, private and compliance-enabled transfers, and measurement of quantum-vulnerable stablecoin exposure.
tldr: A systematization of knowledge on post-quantum stablecoins, mapping quantum vulnerabilities and migration choices across issuer, custody, oracle, bridge, and protocol components.
motivation: Stablecoins concentrate monetary value behind cryptographic keys and inherit quantum vulnerabilities from host chains, consensus, rollups, and privacy systems, creating a need for a stablecoin-specific threat model and migration framework.
method: The authors develop a stablecoin-specific quantum threat model, map cryptographic dependencies to monetary control surfaces, and classify migration choices along authority, location, and hybrid/native/encapsulation dimensions.
result: They identify an authority-liability gap between parties able to migrate components and those bearing losses, and highlight open problems in aggregate and threshold authorization, operation-specific security levels, dormant supply, and exposure measurement.
conclusion: The paper argues that post-quantum stablecoin migration requires coordinated cryptographic, regulatory, and interoperability research, with explicit attention to redemption, continuity, and intervention requirements.

title: Two-Sided Product Expanding Codes Via Rademacher Matrices
authors: Eshan Chattopadhyay, Noam Ringach, Nicholas Spooner
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a proof of the existence of two-sided product expanding codes which, unlike the earlier result of Kalachev and Panteleev (FOCS, 2025), does not rely on explicit constructions of asymptotically optimal locally testable codes ([MATH]-LTCs). For every fixed number of component codes and dimensions whose rates are bounded away from zero and one, we show that independent random linear codes over a sufficiently large prime field have constant two-sided product expansion with probability tending to one. The tradeoff is that our proof requires the characteristic to grow with the block length, while [KP25] takes extensions of [MATH]. To replace the use of [MATH]-LTCs, we develop several new techniques that we view as interesting in their own right. Instead of working directly over finite fields, we work over the reals and use random Rademacher matrices for the generator matrices of the component codes. From here, we we show that the extendability of [MATH]-closed sets can be reduced to controlling the operator norm of sparse restrictions of carefully chosen Gram matrices. Applying the trace power method to bound this norm reduces to bounding the number of possible labelings of certain closed walks on bipartite graphs, which we bound using the sparsity of the operators and bounds on the number of equivalence classes of weak Wigner words from Anderson and Zeitouni (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields., 2006), which were originally applied to band matrices. Due to our techniques not relying on explicit [MATH]-LTCs, we believe that they form a promising starting point towards showing the existence of product expanding tensor codes where the component codes have non-trivial automorphism groups and coboundary expanding codes that could be used as the local codes of non-cubical complexes, such as simplicial complexes.
tldr: The paper proves the existence of two-sided product expanding codes using random Rademacher matrices over the reals, avoiding reliance on explicit asymptotically optimal locally testable codes.
motivation: Prior work (Kalachev–Panteleev, FOCS 2025) established two-sided product expanding codes but depended on explicit constructions of asymptotically optimal LTCs, which limits generalization to other product code settings.
method: Component code generator matrices are replaced by random Rademacher matrices, reducing extendability of closed sets to bounding the operator norm of sparse restrictions of Gram matrices via the trace power method, ultimately counting labelings of closed walks on bipartite graphs using weak Wigner word equivalence classes.
result: For any fixed number of component codes with rates bounded away from 0 and 1, independent random linear codes over a sufficiently large prime field yield constant two-sided product expansion with probability tending to one, at the cost of requiring the field characteristic to grow with block length.
conclusion: The techniques provide a promising route toward product expanding tensor codes with component codes having non-trivial automorphism groups, and toward coboundary expanding codes usable as local codes of non-cubical complexes such as simplicial complexes.

title: Rateless Nested Lattice Codes For Secure Cooperative V2x Broadcast Over Fading And Erasure Channels
authors: Pegah Sharifi, Hassan Khodaiemehr, Khadijeh Bagheri, Chen Feng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) sidelink and uplink broadcast must deliver safety-critical and application-layer data reliably under fast time-varying fading, intermittent packet erasures, and exposure to passive eavesdroppers. Fixed-rate physical-layer codes are poorly matched to these conditions because link quality and the number of successfully received symbols vary across vehicles and over time. This paper proposes a unified vehicular communication framework that combines rateless Construction-D' Raptor lattices, nested-lattice physical-layer security (PLS) with direct-sequence spread spectrum (DSSS), and blockchain-assisted trust management for decode-and-forward (DF) cooperative relaying. At the physical layer, Raptor codes provide incremental redundancy over unreliable V2X links; multilevel lattice decoding enables power-efficient joint coding and modulation; nested shaping and spread spectrum limit fine-lattice recovery by eavesdroppers; and a distributed ledger records decoding success at relays to support reputation-aware relay selection. We model the vehicular air interface as a block-Rayleigh fading channel with additive Gaussian noise and random symbol erasures, representative of urban V2X sidelink behavior. The proposed code concatenates Luby-transform (LT) codes with quasi-cyclic low-density parity-check (QC-LDPC) precodes within Construction-D', with girth-4 cycle removal on the Tanner graph. AWGN benchmarks show competitive symbol error rate (SER) and improved frame error rate (FER) versus matched-length LDPC and LDLC lattices. Under block-Rayleigh fading with erasures, for n=995 at average VNR of 1.5 dB and erasure probability 0.15, rateless Raptor reception achieves 0.3% outage with about 2.3 packets on average, outperforming LDLC and LDPC under identical channels, while an eavesdropper with 8 dB combined SNR and spreading loss fails in 62% of sessions.
tldr: A classical coding framework combining rateless Raptor codes, nested-lattice physical-layer security, and blockchain-assisted trust management for reliable and secure V2X broadcast over fading and erasure channels.
motivation: V2X sidelink and uplink broadcast must be reliable under fast time-varying fading, packet erasures, and eavesdropping, conditions for which fixed-rate physical-layer codes are poorly suited.
method: The authors concatenate Luby-transform codes with QC-LDPC precodes inside Construction-D' Raptor lattices, add nested-lattice PLS with DSSS, and use a distributed ledger to support reputation-aware decode-and-forward relay selection.
result: Under block-Rayleigh fading with erasures at n=995, VNR 1.5 dB and erasure probability 0.15, rateless Raptor reception achieves 0.3% outage with about 2.3 packets on average, outperforming LDLC and LDPC, while an eavesdropper with 8 dB combined SNR and spreading loss fails in 62% of sessions.
conclusion: The proposed rateless nested-lattice scheme offers a practical, secure, and spectrally efficient solution for cooperative V2X broadcast, though it is a classical communications contribution rather than a quantum information result.

title: Einstein--Langevin Source Correlations In Closed Non-relativistic Systems
authors: Li-E Qiang Peng Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic semiclassical gravity represents stress--energy fluctuations through the Einstein--Langevin noise kernel. We examine its Newtonian projection for specified closed, particle-number-conserving non-relativistic sources and distinguish the source covariance from a reduced matter channel. The connected one-particle covariance is state dependent and differs from the universal potential-noise law postulated in the Di\'osi--Penrose model. To relate the source spectrum to dephasing, we define a separate static probe subject to a prescribed Gaussian noise law. For a finite-variance source operator in an isolated non-degenerate eigenstate, the full connected spectral measure has a gap around zero. The probe dephasing exponent is then bounded and its long-time slope vanishes. Stationary doublets can instead carry static or low-frequency spectral lines, while a specified freely spreading Gaussian source gives a finite limiting exponent. Continuum results depend on preparation, normalisation, infrared regularisation and the order of limits. We also compare coherent and incoherent many-body preparations and establish no-signalling for fixed classical-noise channels. These results identify the spatial, temporal and dynamical assumptions needed to relate source fluctuations to a matter-decoherence model. They do not exclude Markovian limits in other number-conserving non-relativistic preparations.
tldr: The paper analyzes Einstein-Langevin source correlations in closed non-relativistic systems and relates them to probe dephasing, finding state-dependent spectral gaps that differ from the Diósi-Penrose universal noise law.
motivation: To clarify the assumptions needed to connect stress-energy fluctuations in stochastic semiclassical gravity to gravitational decoherence models.
method: It computes the connected one-particle covariance and spectral measure for closed particle-number-conserving non-relativistic sources, then studies a static probe subject to prescribed Gaussian noise and compares coherent and incoherent many-body preparations.
result: For a finite-variance source in an isolated non-degenerate eigenstate, the full connected spectral measure has a gap around zero, bounding the probe dephasing exponent and making its long-time slope vanish; stationary doublets or spreading Gaussian sources can still produce low-frequency lines or a finite limiting exponent.
conclusion: Relating source fluctuations to matter decoherence requires specifying spatial, temporal, and dynamical assumptions; no-signalling holds for fixed classical-noise channels, and Markovian limits are not excluded for other number-conserving non-relativistic preparations.

title: A Polynomial-Scaling Pde Solver With Entanglement-Basis Tensor Networks
authors: Abhijatmedhi Chotrattanapituk, Michael J. Landry, Chu-Liang Fu, Mingda Li
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a finite element method (FEM) for partial differential equation (PDE) solver based on the entanglement-basis representation introduced in our companion work. By lifting non-linear finite-element equations into an augmented coefficient space, the governing PDE together with boundary, initial, and inter-element constraints can be expressed through a unified quadratic residual minimization. Although this augmented space grows exponentially with the number of elements, its tensor-product structure allows it to be represented efficiently using tensor networks. Using the matrix product state (MPS) as a concrete example, we show that density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) sweeps enable element-by-element optimization without explicitly constructing the full augmented space. For bounded bond dimension, the resulting computational cost scales polynomially with the number of finite elements. We extend the framework to time-dependent problems through implicit temporal discretization and demonstrate convergence under both mesh and polynomial refinement using diffusion equations.
tldr: The paper develops a finite element method for solving PDEs by representing the augmented coefficient space as a matrix product state tensor network optimized via DMRG sweeps, achieving polynomial scaling in the number of elements.
motivation: Solving PDEs with classical finite element methods becomes prohibitively expensive as the augmented system scales exponentially with the number of elements, motivating an efficient tensor-network representation of the structured solution space.
method: Non-linear finite-element equations with boundary, initial, and inter-element constraints are lifted into an augmented coefficient space expressed as a unified quadratic residual minimization, then represented with an MPS and optimized element-by-element using DMRG sweeps; time dependence is handled via implicit temporal discretization.
result: For bounded bond dimension the computational cost scales polynomially with the number of finite elements, and the framework converges under both mesh and polynomial refinement on diffusion-equation benchmarks.
conclusion: Entanglement-basis tensor networks provide a scalable numerical framework for PDE solving, though the work is a numerical methods contribution rather than a quantum information or thermodynamics result.

title: Orthogonality, Spectral Filling, And Uncertainty
authors: Travis Alvarez, Trevor Camper, Mishko Mitkovski
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let a normalized continuous Parseval frame describe the phase space of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. The frame coefficients of an orthonormal family have total mass equal to the number of states and pointwise mass at most one. This elementary exclusion principle gives explicit lower bounds for the total cost of a family in terms of the volume of low-cost regions. For radial costs, it yields collective mean-dispersion, umbrella, and transport inequalities. The same argument applies to normalized Bessel families, with the Bessel bound measuring the permitted overlap. We also consider semiclassical families for which the frame measures vary. Weak convergence of the normalized measures, together with averaged localization of the normalized kernels, yields continuous-symbol Szeg limits and sharp asymptotics for the lowest Toeplitz energies. The results apply to Bargmann--Fock and weighted Bergman spaces, Gabor and Paley--Wiener spaces, and orthogonal-polynomial and determinantal ensembles, including the GUE.
tldr: The paper establishes an exclusion principle for frame coefficients of orthonormal families, yielding cost lower bounds, uncertainty inequalities, and semiclassical Szegő/Toeplitz asymptotics in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces.
motivation: To understand how orthogonality and spectral filling impose uncertainty and cost constraints in phase-space representations.
method: Uses normalized continuous Parseval frames, Bessel families, and semiclassical analysis of frame measures and kernels.
result: Derives collective mean-dispersion, umbrella, transport inequalities, and continuous-symbol Szegő limits with sharp Toeplitz energy asymptotics; applications to Bargmann-Fock, Bergman, Gabor, Paley-Wiener spaces, and GUE.
conclusion: Provides a unified framework linking orthogonality, uncertainty, and spectral filling with applications to function spaces and random matrix ensembles.

title: Design Automation For Gray-Code Quantum Read-Only Memory
authors: Hao-Yu Lu, Yu-Ting Kao, Yeong-Jar Chang, Chao-Hung Wang, Darsen D. Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a programmable quantum read-only memory based on Gray code encoding, termed GQROM, designed to efficiently load classical data into quantum circuits. This architecture mitigates critical bottlenecks in near-term quantum computing by reducing initialization overhead and gate-induced errors. By utilizing Gray code, in which consecutive addresses differ by only a single bit, GQROM minimizes state transition complexity. We demonstrate the architecture's flexibility in accessing targeted data through initial-state modification. The entire design, including a systematic EDA flow, was implemented and validated on the Qiskit platform, confirming its practical feasibility. These results underscore GQROM's potential as a scalable and hardware-friendly solution for efficient state preparation in quantum circuits.
tldr: The paper proposes GQROM, a Gray-code-encoded programmable quantum read-only memory architecture for loading classical data into quantum circuits with reduced initialization overhead and gate errors.
motivation: Efficiently loading classical data into quantum circuits is a critical bottleneck in near-term quantum computing, where initialization overhead and gate-induced errors limit practical scalability.
method: The authors design a Gray-code-based quantum ROM architecture and a systematic EDA flow, implementing and validating the design on the Qiskit platform.
result: GQROM minimizes state transition complexity via Gray code encoding, enables flexible targeted data access through initial-state modification, and demonstrates practical feasibility on Qiskit.
conclusion: The proposed architecture shows potential as a scalable and hardware-friendly solution for efficient state preparation in quantum circuits.

title: Interaction-induced Period Shift Of The Kohn Oscillation In A Parity-time-symmetric Harmonic Trap
authors: Mingshu Zhao Gaoqing Meng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The center of mass of a Bose--Einstein condensate in a harmonic trap oscillates at the trap frequency independently of the interactions. Without interactions a parity-time-symmetric gain-loss gradient leaves this frequency unchanged, and a cloud of the ground-state width is translated rigidly while the atom number is periodically modulated. With interactions the protection is lost, because the gain and the loss change the number of atoms; the modulated atom number drives the width of the cloud, and the width acts back on the center of mass. At small gain the period grows quadratically with the gain strength, with a coefficient that in the Thomas--Fermi regime is set by the size of the cloud alone. The family of periodic orbits continued from the Kohn oscillation can be followed up to a critical gain, where it comes into resonance with highly excited states of the trap, and over the computed families this critical gain decreases with the amplitude of the oscillation and with the size of the cloud. A five-variable moment model reproduces the period and the width of the cloud along the orbits nearly up to the critical gain.
tldr: The paper studies how interactions modify the period of the Kohn oscillation of a Bose-Einstein condensate in a parity-time-symmetric harmonic trap with gain and loss.
motivation: To understand whether the interaction-independent Kohn oscillation frequency is protected in a non-Hermitian PT-symmetric trap and how gain/loss-induced atom number modulation affects the center-of-mass dynamics.
method: A five-variable moment model is used to describe the coupled dynamics of center-of-mass, width, and atom number, with analytical and numerical continuation of periodic orbits.
result: At small gain, the period increases quadratically with gain strength; the family of periodic orbits persists up to a critical gain where it resonates with highly excited trap states, and the critical gain decreases with oscillation amplitude and cloud size.
conclusion: Interactions break the protection of the Kohn frequency in PT-symmetric traps due to gain/loss-induced atom-number modulation, and the moment model captures the behavior nearly up to the critical gain.

title: Unifying Privacy Accounting: Information Equivalence And Information Loss
authors: Buxin Su, Qiaoshi Yang, Yiding Su, Chendi Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Differential privacy (DP) admits several notions, but the choice among them may affect both privacy analysis and utility. In this paper, we consider four mainstream curve-based privacy notions within a unified information-theoretic framework. For a fixed ordered pair of output distributions, we establish information equivalence among the two directional privacy profiles of [MATH]-DP, the pair of hypothesis-testing trade-off functions, and the extended privacy-loss distribution. The exact R\'enyi differential privacy (RDP) curve joins this equivalence class whenever it is finite at some order greater than one. Under this mild condition, choosing among these notions changes only their semantic interpretation and computational requirements. In contrast, taking the maximum of the directional privacy profiles or compressing the RDP curve into a single zero-concentrated differential privacy (zCDP) parameter can lose information. We quantify the information loss between the exact RDP curve and its zCDP bound for standard noise mechanisms. This gap is zero for Gaussian noise but generally positive for Gaussian-mixture, Laplace, discrete Gaussian, and Poisson-subsampled Gaussian mechanisms. Moreover, this gap grows linearly with the number of independently composed mechanisms. Our information-theoretic perspective has practical consequences. At the same certified privacy level, retaining the full RDP curve rather than using zCDP reduces the required noise variance by up to [MATH] for Gaussian-mixture noise in workloads comparable in size to the American Community Survey. For DP-SGD on Fashion-MNIST under Poisson subsampling, an RDP-based privacy accountant improves test accuracy by up to [MATH] percentage points compared to a zCDP-based accountant when both are calibrated to the same [MATH] guarantee.
tldr: This paper unifies four curve-based differential privacy notions via information equivalence and quantifies information loss when compressing RDP curves to zCDP.
motivation: Differential privacy offers several notions, but choosing among them affects privacy analysis and utility; a unified information-theoretic understanding is needed.
method: The authors establish information equivalence between directional privacy profiles, hypothesis-testing trade-off functions, and extended privacy-loss distributions, and compare exact RDP curves with zCDP bounds for standard noise mechanisms.
result: They show equivalence holds under mild conditions, but max directional profiles or zCDP compression lose information; the RDP–zCDP gap is zero for Gaussian noise but positive for other mechanisms and grows linearly with composition.
conclusion: Retaining full RDP curves can reduce required noise and improve DP-SGD accuracy compared to zCDP accountants at the same privacy guarantee.

title: Where Quantum Fourier Sampling Stops Short: A Three-Gate Audit Protocol For Delay-PUF Security Models
authors: Owen Friedewald, Ali Shiri Sichani, Chi-Ren Shyu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Fourier sampling may help audit the spectral learnability of delay-based physical unclonable functions (PUFs). We ask whether that promise survives access matching, a strong classical comparator, and oracle synthesis. Three gates structure the evaluation. Structure: low degree is not small support at reachable challenge lengths; for 4-XOR at [MATH], degree [MATH] admits [MATH] of all [MATH] characters and the median [MATH]-mass set spans a third of the spectrum. Algorithmics: constructing the phase oracle logically implies classical membership access, making Kushilevitz--Mansour the correct baseline; across 45 tasks it exhausts each finite domain, and no 4-XOR ideal-sampling case reaches [MATH] mass within [MATH] calls. A quantum-kernel diagnostic appears more favorable, with geometric difference rising to [MATH] at [MATH] challenges, but it correlates [MATH] with [MATH] for the classical Gram matrix [MATH], and the 4-XOR label-complexity ratio does not exceed a balance-preserving permutation null ([MATH]). Trace-normalized geometric difference can therefore grow through classical ill-conditioning alone, without task-label alignment. Implementation: a simulator-validated fixed-point phase oracle based on the quantum Fourier transform admits an [MATH] routed-depth reduction, yet the least certified precisions have estimated durations of [MATH]--[MATH] the median dephasing time [MATH] of the mapped qubits on a static backend snapshot, without hardware execution. We find no end-to-end advantage in the evaluated regime, although ideal sampling does use fewer coherent calls on the thresholded task. The contribution is the Three-Gate Quantum Audit Protocol: a reproducible procedure separating an ideal query advantage from a realizable security benefit. This is not a claim about deployed silicon and not an impossibility result.
tldr: The paper introduces a three-gate audit protocol to evaluate whether quantum Fourier sampling provides a realizable security advantage for delay-based PUFs, finding no end-to-end advantage in the evaluated regime.
motivation: Quantum Fourier sampling has been proposed to audit the spectral learnability of delay-based PUFs, but its practical benefit under access matching, classical baselines, and oracle synthesis remains unclear.
method: The authors structure evaluation via three gates: structural analysis of 4-XOR degree versus support, algorithmic comparison with Kushilevitz–Mansour and quantum-kernel diagnostics, and implementation of a simulator-validated fixed-point QFT phase oracle with resource estimates.
result: Classical membership access is implied by phase oracle construction; no 4-XOR ideal sampling reaches target mass within given calls; geometric difference correlates with classical Gram matrix ill-conditioning; QFT oracle requires precisions exceeding dephasing times.
conclusion: No end-to-end advantage is found, though ideal sampling uses fewer coherent calls; the protocol separates ideal query advantage from realizable security benefit.

title: Quasiparticle Quantum Simulation Of Materials With The Bethe-Salpeter Equation
authors: Jielun Chen, Jiace Sun, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02916v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The first-principles quantum simulation of the full electronic Hamiltonian of a material model of realistic size appears daunting even in a future era of fully fault-tolerant quantum computers. In contrast, classical simulations of material excited states rely on heuristic quasiparticle frameworks, such as the GW approximation and Bethe-Salpeter equation, where only a few quasiparticles are explicitly considered. Here we give a detailed description of quasiparticle quantum simulation for multi-excitonic states within the BSE. We develop an explicit first-quantized, orbital-based block encoding of the multi-exciton BSE Hamiltonian for qubitization, and reduce its cost using integral factorization and crystal symmetries. For a materials model of size [MATH], and a fixed number of quasiparticles, the resulting algorithms require [MATH] Toffoli gates and [MATH] logical qubits, or, using space-time tradeoffs, [MATH] Toffoli gates and [MATH] logical qubits, achieving up to a sixth power reduction in Toffoli count, or up to exponential reduction in qubit count, versus standard full Hamiltonian simulation techniques that have been explored in materials simulation. Resource estimates for the classically challenging problem of triexcitonic eigenvalue estimation across a range of semiconductor models of a realistic physical size of [MATH] atoms, show that our Toffoli-optimized implementation reduces the Toffoli count by [MATH] relative to full Hamiltonian simulation estimates, while a qubit-optimized implementation requires only a few hundred logical qubits. More broadly, these results show that classical heuristic frameworks will be essential in the design of future fault-tolerant quantum algorithms for materials.
tldr: The paper develops a quasiparticle quantum simulation approach for multi-excitonic states using the Bethe-Salpeter equation, with block encoding and resource estimates for fault-tolerant quantum algorithms.
motivation: Full first-principles quantum simulation of realistic material Hamiltonians is daunting, while classical heuristic quasiparticle frameworks like GW and BSE consider only a few quasiparticles.
method: A first-quantized, orbital-based block encoding of the multi-exciton BSE Hamiltonian is constructed for qubitization, with cost reduced via integral factorization and crystal symmetries.
result: The algorithms achieve up to a sixth-power reduction in Toffoli count or exponential reduction in qubit count versus full Hamiltonian simulation, with resource estimates for triexcitonic eigenvalue estimation across semiconductor models.
conclusion: Classical heuristic frameworks such as BSE will be essential in designing future fault-tolerant quantum algorithms for materials.

title: Robust Constrained Optimization Of Nonequilibrium Casimir Repulsion In A Biased-semiconductor Cavity
authors: Belkacem E. Khodja Mohamed R. Khodja
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonequilibrium electromagnetic fluctuations offer a route to repulsive Casimir--Lifshitz forces. However, designs optimized only at nominal conditions may be fragile. We formulate repulsion in a planar PEC--vacuum--biased-GaAs--vacuum--PEC stack as a robust constrained optimization problem. The smaller of the outward pressures on the two conductors is maximized under fabrication and drive uncertainties. In the optically thick-slab limit, we prove that identical boundaries admit a symmetric optimizer, so equality of the optimal gaps emerges from the model rather than being imposed. At [MATH], with gap uncertainty of [MATH] and drive uncertainty of [MATH], the optimized design sustains a worst-case outward pressure of [MATH] and exceeds the corresponding far-field radiation-pressure plateau by [MATH]. At the nominal and active worst-case points, a full finite-slab scattering calculation agrees with the reduced model to within [MATH]. These results provide a design bound for cavity-enhanced nonequilibrium Casimir--Lifshitz repulsion and show how robust optimization can distinguish cavity enhancement from ordinary far-field radiation pressure.
tldr: The paper formulates and solves a robust constrained optimization problem for enhancing repulsive nonequilibrium Casimir-Lifshitz forces in a biased-semiconductor planar cavity under fabrication and drive uncertainties.
motivation: Nonequilibrium electromagnetic fluctuations can produce repulsive Casimir forces, but designs optimized only at nominal conditions may be fragile to real-world uncertainties.
method: The authors model a planar PEC-vacuum-biased-GaAs-vacuum-PEC stack, derive a symmetric optimizer in the optically thick-slab limit, and perform finite-slab scattering calculations to validate the reduced model.
result: The optimized design sustains a worst-case outward pressure that exceeds the far-field radiation-pressure plateau, with finite-slab calculations agreeing with the reduced model at nominal and active worst-case points.
conclusion: The work provides a design bound for cavity-enhanced nonequilibrium Casimir-Lifshitz repulsion and shows how robust optimization can distinguish cavity enhancement from ordinary far-field radiation pressure.

title: Digital Twin For Full Field-of-view Fraunhofer Holographic Patterning
authors: Antoni J. Wojcik, Dilawer Singh, Hannah J. Joyce, Timothy D. Wilkinson
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02518v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computer-generated holography allows for nearly complete dynamic control of optical fields, but discrepancies between idealised propagation models and physical hardware limit its performance, particularly across large fields of view. We present a compact differentiable model of a Fraunhofer holographic projector which describes the complete propagation chain, from a phase-only spatial light modulator (SLM) to the camera recording the focal plane of a Fourier lens. It uses physically interpretable parameters for the SLM, illumination, pupil, coherent stray light, and camera. The model is identified in situ from noise-probed hologram-image pairs without additional hardware, system modification, or camera-in-the-loop refinement. The recovered digital twin is used to generate holograms for patterns spanning the entire first diffraction order of the SLM at its spatial-bandwidth limit. This full-field capability is enabled by measuring field-dependent pupil aberrations and compensating severe inter-pixel crosstalk by operating at the [MATH] phase modulation range. The stray light responsible for residual zeroth-order artefacts is recovered in amplitude and phase, allowing its physical origin to be investigated, and its contribution suppressed during hologram synthesis. The work establishes a framework for calibration-aware field synthesis in holographic systems operating in the Fraunhofer regime for applications such as maskless lithography and optical tweezer arrays.
tldr: A compact differentiable digital twin of a Fraunhofer holographic projector is identified in situ to enable full field-of-view hologram generation at the spatial-bandwidth limit.
motivation: Idealized propagation models fail to capture hardware imperfections across large fields of view, limiting the performance of computer-generated holography for applications like maskless lithography and optical tweezer arrays.
method: The authors build a physically interpretable model of the full optical chain—SLM, illumination, pupil, coherent stray light, and camera—and identify its parameters from noise-probed hologram-image pairs without extra hardware or camera-in-the-loop refinement.
result: The recovered digital twin measures field-dependent pupil aberrations, compensates severe inter-pixel crosstalk by operating at a specific phase modulation range, and suppresses residual zeroth-order stray light, enabling holograms across the entire first diffraction order.
conclusion: This establishes a calibration-aware framework for full-field holographic synthesis in the Fraunhofer regime, with potential impact on maskless lithography and optical tweezer arrays.

title: Structural Crossover Of Complex Networks: Bridging Degree Correlation And Fractality
authors: Shogo Mizutaka, Jun Yamamoto, Kousuke Yakubo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the relationship between long-range degree correlations and fractality in scale-free random networks. By analyzing degree correlations in scale-free random networks at the percolation threshold, at which a giant component emerges, we derive the ball volume [MATH], defined as the average number of nodes within distance [MATH] from a root node with degree [MATH]. The resulting expression predicts a degree-dependent structural crossover. For [MATH], the ball volume grows as [MATH], whereas for [MATH], it crosses over to the global fractal scaling [MATH]. Here, [MATH] is the fractal dimension of critical scale-free random networks. We further show that the structural crossover can be naturally understood in terms of critical branching processes and is also observed in empirical fractal networks.
tldr: This paper analyzes degree correlations in scale-free random networks at the percolation threshold to derive a degree-dependent structural crossover between local ball-volume growth and global fractal scaling.
motivation: The relationship between long-range degree correlations and fractality in complex scale-free networks is not fully understood, motivating a quantitative connection between these structural features.
method: The authors analytically derive the average ball volume for a root node of given degree in scale-free random networks at criticality, then interpret the resulting crossover via critical branching processes and compare with empirical fractal networks.
result: They find that for small distances the ball volume grows with a degree-dependent exponent, while beyond a crossover scale it recovers the global fractal scaling characterized by the network's fractal dimension.
conclusion: The structural crossover provides a bridge between degree correlation and fractality in complex networks, and the same behavior is observed in empirical fractal networks.

title: Duplication-Aware Retiming And Cell Interface Redesign For Superconductor Circuit Minimization
authors: Panagiotis Papanikolaou, Alex Vanasse, Haoran Jin, Georgios Tzimpragos, Jennifer Volk
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconductor electronics have increasingly shifted away from RSFQ and its variants toward logic families that eliminate explicit gate-level clocking. While this transition enables simpler circuits and more efficient architectures, it also introduces an implicit reliance on dual-rail codes, resulting in inherent gate duplication. This work presents a duplication-aware retiming methodology for Josephson junction (JJ) count minimization, co-optimizing register placement and polarity assignment. The approach applies beyond SFQ to any monotonic circuit. We further identify cell interfaces---specifically, interconnect drivers, receivers, and fanout (FO) elements---as dominant contributors to JJ count in each cell. A new amplifier design is introduced to reduce these costs, integrated within existing SFQ cells, experimentally verified, and characterized to form a new SFQ cell library. Our results demonstrate a 63-71% JJ count reduction in single-cycle implementations and 41-66% reduction in multi-cycle implementations compared to the prior state-of-the-art. The latter establishes a new Pareto frontier, achieving both shorter critical paths and lower JJ counts than the best-to-date single-cycle implementations.
tldr: A duplication-aware retiming and cell interface redesign methodology reduces Josephson junction count in superconductor SFQ circuits by 41–71%.
motivation: Superconductor electronics are shifting to logic families without explicit gate-level clocking, but this introduces dual-rail codes and inherent gate duplication, making JJ count minimization critical for efficient circuits.
method: The authors develop a duplication-aware retiming approach that co-optimizes register placement and polarity assignment, and redesign cell interfaces (drivers, receivers, fanout) with a new amplifier integrated into existing SFQ cells, experimentally verified as a new cell library.
result: The method achieves 63–71% JJ count reduction in single-cycle implementations and 41–66% in multi-cycle implementations, establishing a new Pareto frontier with shorter critical paths and lower JJ counts than prior best single-cycle designs.
conclusion: This work provides a practical circuit-level optimization for superconductor logic, but it is not directly connected to quantum information theory, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined in the research interests.

title: Intrinsic Electromagnetic Properties
authors: Eduardo Barredo-Alamilla, Timur Z. Seidov, Daniel A. Bobylev, Maxim A. Gorlach
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02280v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electromagnetic properties of materials are commonly inferred from how they scatter light. Here we show that this diagnostic is fundamentally incomplete. We predict the existence of an intrinsic electromagnetic property that remains invisible in any scattering experiment independently of geometry, polarization, far-field or near-field excitation. Still, this property affects the radiation emitted by the sources embedded inside the material. We reveal this phenomenon for a specially designed nonreciprocal magnetoelectric material combining axion and dual axion responses. Our results establish intrinsic electromagnetic properties as a distinct class of material responses and show that scattering experiments alone are insufficient to characterize matter.
tldr: The paper predicts an intrinsic electromagnetic material property that cannot be detected by any scattering experiment but affects radiation from embedded sources in nonreciprocal magnetoelectric media.
motivation: Electromagnetic material properties are usually inferred from light scattering, but this diagnostic may miss intrinsic responses that are invisible to external probes.
method: The authors theoretically analyze scattering from a specially designed nonreciprocal magnetoelectric material combining axion and dual axion responses, including radiation from embedded sources.
result: They identify an intrinsic electromagnetic property that remains invisible in any scattering geometry, polarization, or near-/far-field excitation, yet modifies emission from embedded sources.
conclusion: Scattering experiments alone are fundamentally insufficient to characterize matter, establishing intrinsic electromagnetic properties as a distinct class of material responses.

title: Performance Of Zero-determinant Strategies In Repeated Games Without Discounting
authors: Masahiko Ueda
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zero-determinant (ZD) strategies are a class of strategies in repeated games, which unilaterally control payoffs. It has been shown that several ZD strategies promote cooperation in social dilemma games. It has been widely believed that the performance of ZD strategies is expressed as ``unilaterally enforce linear relations between payoffs''. However, in order to interpret properties of ZD strategies in repeated games without discounting, previous studies assumed that the limit of the Cesaro average of the probability distribution of the action profile exists. Here, we explain the performance of ZD strategies without this assumption, which leads to a stronger result than previous ones.
tldr: The paper removes a technical assumption (existence of the Cesàro limit of the action-profile distribution) in the analysis of zero-determinant strategies in undiscounted repeated games, yielding a stronger characterization of their payoff-control performance.
motivation: Zero-determinant strategies are known to unilaterally enforce linear payoff relations, but prior analyses in repeated games without discounting relied on assuming the Cesàro average of the action-profile distribution converges, which is an unjustified restriction.
method: The author re-derives the performance characterization of ZD strategies within the framework of undiscounted repeated games using game-theoretic and stochastic-process arguments, dropping the Cesàro-limit assumption.
result: A stronger, assumption-free statement of the linear payoff-relation property of ZD strategies is obtained for undiscounted repeated games.
conclusion: The findings sharpen the theoretical understanding of ZD strategies in repeated games without discounting, with implications for the study of cooperation in social dilemmas.

title: AI-Assisted Gpu Optimization Of The Stochastic Variational Method For Few-Body Boson System
authors: Noritaka Shimizu, Shigeyoshi Aoyama, Yusuke Tsunoda, Akira Nukada
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The stochastic variational method (SVM) is one of the most powerful methods to solve quantum few-body systems precisely in various fields, such as nuclear and atomic physics. To the best of our knowledge, no SVM code optimized for GPUs has been reported. We developed a parallel SVM code for few-body clusters of [MATH]He atoms and optimized it for two GPU architectures, NVIDIA GH200 and AMD Instinct MI300A, with the entire code written by an AI coding agent. On the algorithmic side, we introduce the secular-equation method with the Gu--Eisenstat prescription for solving the generalized eigenvalue problem within the SVM framework. The main part of the code tuning is to batch the many small matrices so that the GPUs are used efficiently, together with an array layout in memory optimized for coalesced addressing. For the five-body system with 4800 SVM basis states, the tuned SVM code runs 16.2 (14.7) times faster on the NVIDIA GH200 (AMD MI300A) than the same tuned code on the Intel Xeon Max CPU system, and 168 (153) times faster than the first working CPU implementation. The achieved performance brings 6-body and larger cluster systems within reach.
tldr: The paper develops a GPU-optimized stochastic variational method (SVM) code for few-body boson systems, with the entire code written by an AI coding agent.
motivation: Few-body systems require precise numerical solutions, and GPU acceleration could enable larger clusters, but no SVM code optimized for GPUs had been reported.
method: They introduce a secular-equation method with the Gu–Eisenstat prescription for solving generalized eigenvalue problems within SVM, and optimize GPU performance by batching many small matrices and using a coalesced memory layout.
result: For a five-body system with 4800 SVM basis states, the tuned code runs 16.2x (14.7x) faster on NVIDIA GH200 (AMD MI300A) than on an Intel Xeon Max CPU system, and 168x (153x) faster than the first working CPU implementation.
conclusion: The AI-assisted GPU optimization significantly accelerates SVM, bringing 6-body and larger cluster systems within reach for few-body physics.

title: Fast Nanophotonic Inverse Design Using Precomputed Numerical Green Functions
authors: Thi Phuong Thao Nguyen, James Wang, Constantine Sideris
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inverse design has been transformative in nanophotonics, providing an automated means of realizing high-performance, non-intuitive devices. However, the primary bottleneck of existing inverse design approaches is their reliance on time-consuming and computationally expensive full-wave electromagnetic simulations. In this work, we extend the Precomputed Numerical Green Function (PNGF) method for the first time to nanophotonic inverse design, accelerating evaluation of the forward problem by multiple orders of magnitude with no loss in accuracy compared to the full-wave solution. After a single, fully parallelizable precomputation step, both the objective function and its gradient can be evaluated through simple calculations whose cost scales linearly with the size of the design region. A low-rank matrix update technique further reduces the cost of objective function evaluation, yielding sub-millisecond computation times per iteration. Design examples using both gradient-based level-set optimization and tile-flipping direct binary search often achieve more than three orders of magnitude speedup in design time, resulting in an ultrafast photonic inverse design platform that can design new devices from scratch in seconds.
tldr: The paper extends the Precomputed Numerical Green Function method to nanophotonic inverse design, achieving orders-of-magnitude speedup by replacing full-wave electromagnetic simulations with cheap linear-scaling evaluations.
motivation: Inverse design in nanophotonics is bottlenecked by the high computational cost of repeated full-wave electromagnetic simulations required for objective and gradient evaluation.
method: The authors adapt the Precomputed Numerical Green Function (PNGF) approach, performing a single fully parallelizable precomputation step so that objective and gradient evaluations scale linearly with design-region size, with a low-rank matrix update further reducing cost.
result: Design examples using level-set gradient optimization and tile-flipping direct binary search achieve over three orders of magnitude speedup, with sub-millisecond per-iteration evaluations and no loss of accuracy versus full-wave solutions.
conclusion: The approach yields an ultrafast photonic inverse design platform capable of designing new devices from scratch in seconds, though it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems research.

title: Metasurface-on-Lithium-Niobate Architecture For Spin-decoupled Second Harmonic Wavefront Shaping
authors: Yiwen Liu, Chao Meng, Sergey I. Bozhevolnyi, Fei Ding
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear metasurfaces (NMSs) enable simultaneous generation and manipulation of harmonic light with ultrathin nanophotonic platforms. However, conventional NMSs typically adopt a monolithic single-layer configuration in which frequency conversion, polarization selection and wavefront engineering are intertwined to simultaneously occur within the same nonlinear meta-atoms, making these functionalities intrinsically interdependent and imposing constraints on material choice, structural symmetry, and the available geometric parameter space. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a metasurface-on-lithium-niobate architecture that physically separates harmonic light generation and wavefront manipulation. In this platform, a z-cut thin-film LN layer serves as a spin-selective second-harmonic source through its intrinsic bulk second-order nonlinearity, while an overlaid dielectric metasurface subsequently and independently molds wavefronts of generated harmonic fields. The two-step process, by virtue of harmonic generation being decoupled from wavefront shaping, removes symmetry constraints associated with conventional nonlinear meta-atoms and enables the direct transfer of well-established linear metasurface design strategies to harmonic wavefront engineering. As proof-of-concept demonstrations, we realize spin-decoupled second-harmonic beam steering and spin-multiplexed holography, achieving high-contrast routing of harmonic signals with orthogonal spin states into distinct diffraction channels and high-fidelity reconstruction of independent holographic images. By redirecting the harmonic wavefront control from the meta-atom engineering to the modular system-level design, our approach establishes a versatile route toward integrated nonlinear meta-optics and provides a scalable platform for advanced optical functionalities.
tldr: A metasurface-on-lithium-niobate architecture that decouples second-harmonic generation from wavefront shaping, enabling spin-decoupled nonlinear beam steering and holography.
motivation: Conventional nonlinear metasurfaces intertwine frequency conversion, polarization selection, and wavefront engineering within single meta-atoms, restricting material choice, symmetry, and design freedom.
method: A z-cut thin-film lithium niobate layer provides spin-selective bulk second-order nonlinearity for harmonic generation, while an overlaid dielectric metasurface independently molds the generated harmonic wavefronts.
result: The authors experimentally demonstrate spin-decoupled second-harmonic beam steering and spin-multiplexed holography with high-contrast routing and high-fidelity image reconstruction.
conclusion: Separating harmonic generation from wavefront control allows linear metasurface design strategies to be transferred to nonlinear optics, offering a scalable modular platform for integrated nonlinear meta-optics.

title: The Monatomic Limit Of Polyatomic Gases As Concentration Of The Internal-energy Measure
authors: Tommaso Ruggeri
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Rational Extended Thermodynamics, the monatomic limit of polyatomic gases is often singular. For the internal-state density [MATH], with [MATH], we prove that the normalized equilibrium distribution of the molecular internal energy [MATH] concentrates at [MATH] as [MATH], providing a rigorous justification of the Dirac prescription and its first-order correction. In classical ET14, the internal-mode energy differs from equilibrium by [MATH]; positivity yields [MATH], while the exact entropy develops a boundary corner at [MATH]. Negative dynamic pressures remain admissible, but fixed negative values do not approach the monatomic state with the prescribed total energy. This explains the need for compatible initial data. In the relativistic case, the internal energy is conditionally gamma distributed at fixed momentum; the constitutive integrals follow directly, and we derive an exact energy identity and the first correction to the Synge energy.
tldr: The paper proves a concentration result for the internal-energy measure in the monatomic limit of polyatomic gases within Rational Extended Thermodynamics, including a relativistic extension.
motivation: In Rational Extended Thermodynamics the monatomic limit of polyatomic gases is often singular, so a rigorous justification of the Dirac prescription and its first-order correction is needed.
method: The authors analyze the normalized equilibrium distribution of molecular internal energy, prove concentration as the model approaches the monatomic limit, and derive constitutive integrals, an exact energy identity, and a first correction to the Synge energy in the relativistic case.
result: The internal energy measure concentrates at zero in the monatomic limit with an explicit first-order correction; negative dynamic pressures are admissible, but fixed negative values do not approach the monatomic state, and the exact entropy develops a boundary corner.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous mathematical foundation for the monatomic limit of polyatomic gases in extended thermodynamics, clarifying compatible initial data and relativistic corrections without addressing quantum information or information-theoretic thermodynamics.

title: Intent-Hiding Jailbreaks: An Information-Theoretic Framework For Compositional Attacks
authors: Ravi Tandon Fengwei Tian
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work has shown that large language models (LLMs) can be vulnerable to jailbreak attacks in which harmful intent is obscured through composition with benign tasks. A harmful request refused in isolation may elicit a different response when embedded within a larger, seemingly benign query. We study these compositional intent-hiding jailbreaks from an information-theoretic perspective. Our formulation associates each task with an estimated probability of being judged harmful: the average over the full task collection defines the prior probability of harmful intent, while the average over a selected bundle containing the target defines the posterior. Selecting auxiliary tasks so that these averages agree, which we call prior-posterior matching, leaves the estimated intent unchanged even though the harmful target remains in the bundle. We study two settings that differ in whether query construction is part of the optimization. In the query-independent setting, tasks are selected without regard to how they will be expressed in the final query. We show that exact prior-posterior matching under a bundle-size constraint is computationally hard, derive an optimal water-filling solution for fractional weights, and characterize the smallest bundle satisfying a prescribed safety threshold. In the query-dependent setting, task selection and query construction are considered jointly, and intent concealment and target preservation are evaluated on the resulting query. We evaluate jailbreak effectiveness and preservation of the target behavior across bundle sizes, query generators, and several open-source models. These results show that compositional queries can elicit target behaviors beyond the direct-request baseline under the evaluated search budgets, while revealing a trade-off: as bundle size increases, response-level target preservation tends to decrease for several models.
tldr: The paper proposes an information-theoretic framework for compositional intent-hiding jailbreak attacks on LLMs, analyzing prior-posterior matching and query construction trade-offs.
motivation: LLMs can be jailbroken by embedding harmful requests in benign task bundles; this work seeks to understand and optimize such intent-hiding composition from an information-theoretic perspective.
method: It models task harmfulness as probabilities, defines prior-posterior matching to conceal intent, studies query-independent and query-dependent settings, derives hardness and water-filling results, and evaluates across models.
result: Exact matching under bundle-size constraints is computationally hard; optimal fractional weights follow water-filling; compositional queries can elicit target behaviors beyond direct requests but target preservation decreases with bundle size.
conclusion: Compositional intent-hiding jailbreaks are effective under search budgets but involve a trade-off between bundle size and response-level target preservation.

title: Non-Malleable Affine Extractors With Small Error And Complexity Lower Bounds
authors: Yan Zhong Xin Li
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct explicit non-malleable affine extractors for every constant entropy rate, with linear output length and exponentially small error, against any fixed number of affine tamperings without fixed points. For every fixed [MATH] and [MATH], we also obtain entropy threshold [MATH], output length [MATH], and error [MATH] against [MATH] tamperings. Our extractors, as well as the directional affine extractors of Li and Zhong (CCC 2024), yield explicit Boolean functions with correlation [MATH] against weakly read-once linear branching programs of size [MATH]. For non-oblivious decision trees, we prove linear depth lower bounds for queries of each fixed degree [MATH]. Applying Li's sumset extractor (FOCS 2023) gives depth [MATH] for growing locality [MATH], where [MATH] is fixed. In the same range, directional affine extractors give correlation [MATH] against local trees of depth [MATH], for a sufficiently small constant [MATH]. Our extractors derandomize the lossless lifting of Efremenko and Itsykson (STOC 2026). For every fixed [MATH], this gives explicit polynomial-size unsatisfiable CNFs on [MATH] variables whose [MATH] refutations of resolution depth at most [MATH] require size at least [MATH]. Separately, parity substitutions give polynomial-size CNFs on [MATH] variables with polynomial-size ordinary-resolution proofs for which every [MATH] refutation of size [MATH] and depth [MATH] satisfies [MATH]. This removes the [MATH] loss in the tradeoff of Itsykson, Podolskii, and Shekhovtsov (CCC 2026).
tldr: Constructs explicit non-malleable affine extractors with small error and uses them to prove complexity lower bounds for branching programs, decision trees, and resolution proofs.
motivation: Non-malleable extractors are a central pseudorandomness primitive, and explicit constructions with optimal parameters are highly sought after; additionally, such extractors can yield lower bounds in computational complexity.
method: The authors build explicit non-malleable affine extractors against a fixed number of affine tamperings without fixed points, and apply parity substitutions and Li's sumset extractor to derandomize lossless lifting and derive query and proof complexity lower bounds.
result: They obtain extractors for every constant entropy rate with linear output length and exponentially small error, correlation bounds against weakly read-once linear branching programs, linear depth lower bounds for non-oblivious decision trees, and polynomial-size CNFs with resolution size-depth tradeoffs.
conclusion: The work improves parameters for non-malleable affine extractors and provides new lower bounds in complexity theory, including derandomizing the lossless lifting of Efremenko and Itsykson and removing a loss in a known resolution tradeoff.

title: Code Distances Of Matrix Rank-metric Codes Under Add-and-Remove Transformations
authors: Gianira N. Alfarano, Rakhi Pratihar, Adrien Vin\c{c}otte
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a matrix rank-metric code [MATH] and an integer [MATH], the [MATH]-th subcode distance of [MATH] is the largest minimum rank distance of an [MATH]-dimensional subcode of [MATH]. We study how subcode distances change under the Add-and-Remove construction, in which a subcode of codimension [MATH] is kept and a space of dimension [MATH] is added; this construction is used, with Gabidulin codes, in the [MATH] signature scheme. For arbitrary matrix codes, we give inequalities between the subcode distances of the original and of the new code, and we show that Delsarte duality interchanges [MATH] and [MATH]. For matrix Gabidulin codes, whose subcode distances are given by an explicit formula, we show that, if [MATH], then within each block of indices [MATH] not exceeding [MATH], all but the last [MATH] subcode distances are the same as for the Gabidulin code, and the remaining ones decrease by at most one; a small example shows that such a decrease can occur. We also express the minimum distance of the new code in terms of the rank distance between the added space and the common subcode. For [MATH], the lower bound on the minimum distance of the dual public code used by the known distinguisher when [MATH] is a special case of these results; for the proposed parameters, where [MATH], the same bound holds for a subcode of codimension [MATH] of the dual public code.
tldr: This paper analyzes how subcode distances of matrix rank-metric codes change under the Add-and-Remove construction, with applications to a code-based signature scheme.
motivation: The Add-and-Remove construction is used with Gabidulin codes in a cryptographic signature scheme, motivating a detailed study of the resulting code parameters.
method: The authors derive inequalities relating subcode distances of the original and transformed codes, show that Delsarte duality interchanges parameters, and obtain explicit formulas for matrix Gabidulin codes.
result: For matrix Gabidulin codes, within each index block not exceeding a bound, all but the last subcode distances are unchanged and the last decreases by at most one; the minimum distance is expressed via the rank distance between the added space and the common subcode.
conclusion: These results generalize known bounds on the dual public code for the signature scheme and clarify parameter choices for cryptographically relevant instances.

title: Graded Twisted Reflection Matrices Of GL-type
authors: A. Mudrov D. Algethami
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify constant numerical solutions of the [MATH]-graded twisted reflection equation for the fundamental [MATH]-type R-matrix and an arbitrary parity sequence, without assuming evenness or invertibility. The classification is based on a four-index locality principle established for this type of reflection equation. We determine the singular and invertible solutions and recover previously conjectured matrices for the minimal symmetric grading. Even invertible solutions comply with the recent classification of graded Satake diagrams. The classical stabilizer of a full-support lower-triangular non-even family is a Lie superalgebra whose even part is an electrical Lie algebra.
tldr: The paper classifies constant numerical solutions of the graded twisted reflection equation for the fundamental GL-type R-matrix, without assuming evenness or invertibility.
motivation: The graded twisted reflection equation is relevant to integrable systems and quantum groups with superalgebraic structures, but the work is primarily a mathematical classification problem.
method: The authors establish a four-index locality principle for this type of reflection equation and use it to classify singular and invertible solutions for arbitrary parity sequences.
result: They recover previously conjectured matrices for the minimal symmetric grading and show that even invertible solutions comply with the classification of graded Satake diagrams.
conclusion: The classical stabilizer of a full-support lower-triangular non-even family is identified as a Lie superalgebra whose even part is an electrical Lie algebra.

title: Critical Behavior Of Stochastic Rumors On The One-dimensional Integer Lattice
authors: Nevena Mari\'c, Aleksandar Mini\'c, Pablo M. Rodriguez
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study rumor-spreading models on the one-dimensional integer lattice, with particular emphasis on the effect of forgetting mechanisms on the long-term behavior of the rumor. We consider the spatial version of the classical Maki--Thompson model together with two variants that incorporate forgetting. Each model is formulated as an interacting particle system and describes the propagation of information through local interactions between neighboring individuals. Our results show that the introduction of forgetting fundamentally changes the behavior of the process. In the classical Maki--Thompson model, the rumor becomes extinct, whereas the two models with forgetting exhibit nontrivial phase transitions between extinction and survival. More precisely, we establish the existence of critical transmission rates that separate regimes in which the rumor dies out almost surely from regimes in which it survives with positive probability. We also investigate the dependence of these critical thresholds on the stifling rate. Combining rigorous arguments with numerical simulations, we prove the existence of the phase transitions, obtain estimates for the critical values, and explore the corresponding phase diagrams. These findings show that forgetting, despite acting as a mechanism that removes spreaders, can qualitatively alter the dynamics of rumor propagation by creating regimes of sustained information spread. Our work provides new insight into the critical behavior of spatial rumor models and raises several questions for future research.
tldr: This paper studies stochastic rumor-spreading models on a one-dimensional lattice with forgetting mechanisms, showing that forgetting induces nontrivial phase transitions between extinction and survival.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how forgetting alters long-term information propagation in spatial rumor models, specifically extending the classical Maki-Thompson model.
method: They formulate several variants as interacting particle systems on the one-dimensional integer lattice and combine rigorous mathematical proofs with numerical simulations to analyze critical behavior.
result: The classical Maki-Thompson model always leads to rumor extinction, whereas the variants with forgetting exhibit phase transitions at critical transmission rates, with thresholds depending on the stifling rate.
conclusion: Forgetting, despite removing spreaders, can qualitatively change rumor dynamics and create regimes of sustained information spread, opening questions for future research.

title: Fully Coupled Nonlinear Mean-Field FBS{\Delta}Es: Solvability And An Lq Buffer-Adjustment Illustration
authors: Yingjie Zheng, Qingxin Meng, Maoning Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes sufficient conditions for finite-horizon solvability of fully coupled nonlinear mean-field forward--backward stochastic difference equations with dependence on unconditional first moments. The forward recursion uses conditional projections of the next backward state and its product with the innovation. Building on existing domination--monotonicity methods, we formulate deterministic matrix combinations in centered and mean coordinates and prove a continuation estimate uniform in the homotopy parameter. Global Lipschitz continuity and one active domination--coercivity direction yield a unique square-integrable adapted solution, an a priori bound, and coefficient stability. The active parameter can be normalized without imposing an additional smallness restriction on the original coefficients. A sign transformation handles the opposite monotonicity orientation. A nonlinear example with saturating state and mean interactions verifies the assumptions, including degenerate domination directions. A scalar mean-field LQ buffer-adjustment model illustrates the theorem: its Hamiltonian solution characterizes the unique open-loop optimizer. An exact finite scenario-tree calculation checks this characterization against direct quadratic optimization.
tldr: The paper establishes sufficient conditions for finite-horizon solvability of fully coupled nonlinear mean-field forward-backward stochastic difference equations and illustrates them with a linear-quadratic buffer-adjustment model.
motivation: Fully coupled nonlinear mean-field forward-backward stochastic difference equations with dependence on unconditional first moments are challenging to solve, especially for finite-horizon problems.
method: The authors use domination-monotonicity methods, deterministic matrix combinations in centered and mean coordinates, and a uniform continuation estimate to prove existence, uniqueness, and stability.
result: Under global Lipschitz continuity and one active domination-coercivity direction, they obtain a unique square-integrable adapted solution, an a priori bound, and coefficient stability; a nonlinear example and an exact finite scenario-tree calculation validate the characterization.
conclusion: The work provides a solvability theory for a class of mean-field stochastic difference equations and demonstrates its applicability to linear-quadratic buffer-adjustment problems.

title: The Double Covering Of Compact Quantum Group $SO_q(4)$
authors: Bipul Saurabh
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that [MATH] is a quantum normal subgroup of [MATH] and that the quotient group is isomorphic to [MATH], thereby establishing that [MATH] is a double cover of [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves that a certain compact quantum group is a quantum normal subgroup of another compact quantum group, with quotient isomorphic to a third, establishing a double covering relation for SO_q(4).
motivation: The study of compact quantum groups and their subgroup structures is a purely mathematical topic in quantum group theory, motivated by extending classical Lie group covering relations to the quantum deformation setting.
method: The author uses the algebraic framework of compact quantum groups, analyzing quantum normal subgroups, quotient quantum groups, and isomorphisms to construct and verify the double covering relation.
result: It is shown that the quotient of the larger compact quantum group by the quantum normal subgroup is isomorphic to the relevant quantum group, yielding that the subgroup is a double cover of SO_q(4).
conclusion: The paper establishes a quantum analogue of the classical double covering for SO_q(4), contributing to the structure theory of compact quantum groups.

title: From Continuous To Fully Discrete Carleman Estimates: A Transfer Principle For Parabolic Schemes
authors: Yu Wang Qi L\"u
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Direct approaches to discrete parabolic Carleman estimates often rely on weighted identities tailored to the discrete operator. We prove an abstract transfer theorem that derives such estimates for fully discrete backward Euler schemes with conforming spatial reconstructions from a continuous Carleman inequality together with suitable weighted approximation and compatibility properties. For a class of time-independent positive self-adjoint operators, the key construction assigns to each discrete state a shifted continuous auxiliary problem whose discrete solution is exactly the prescribed state. Weighted space-time error estimates, uniform over the full discrete load space, then transfer the inequality while preserving the residual and observation terms of the original scheme. This separates the PDE-specific Carleman analysis from the numerical verification required for each discretization. We verify the hypotheses for the heat equation discretized by consistent-mass [MATH] finite elements on locally graded meshes in two and three dimensions and by standard Cartesian finite differences in any fixed dimension. For the heat equation, the transferred estimate is valid for Carleman parameters up to the scale [MATH]. For bounded real-valued space-time potentials, the resulting estimates yield relaxed observability and approximate null controls with uniformly bounded cost and exponentially small terminal errors under independent spatial and temporal refinement; weak accumulation points of the reconstructed controls are continuous null controls.
tldr: The paper proves an abstract transfer principle that derives fully discrete parabolic Carleman estimates for backward Euler schemes from continuous Carleman inequalities, verified for finite-element and finite-difference discretizations of the heat equation.
motivation: Direct discrete Carleman estimates typically require weighted identities tailored to each discrete operator, making the analysis PDE- and discretization-specific and hard to reuse.
method: An abstract transfer theorem maps each discrete state to a shifted continuous auxiliary problem whose discrete solution matches the prescribed state, using weighted approximation and compatibility properties to carry the continuous Carleman inequality over to the discrete setting while preserving residual and observation terms.
result: The hypotheses are verified for consistent-mass finite elements on locally graded meshes in 2D/3D and for Cartesian finite differences in any fixed dimension, with the estimate valid up to a certain Carleman parameter scale; bounded space-time potentials yield relaxed observability and approximate null controls with uniformly bounded cost and exponentially small terminal errors.
conclusion: The transfer principle cleanly separates PDE-specific Carleman analysis from discretization-specific verification, providing a general route to discrete Carleman estimates and controllability results for parabolic schemes.

title: From Ts-suf-2 To Ts-suf-4: Practical Security Enhancements For Frost2 Threshold Signatures
authors: Will Wang, Syh-Yuan Tan, Ryan Chow, Chanson Chan, Martin Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Threshold signature schemes play a vital role in securing digital assets within blockchain and distributed systems. FROST2 stands out as a practical threshold Schnorr signature scheme, noted for its efficiency and compatibility with standard verification processes. However, under the one-more discrete logarithm assumption, with static corruption and centralized key generation settings, FROST2 has been shown by Bellare et al. (in CRYPTO 2022) to achieve only TS-SUF-2 security, which is a consequence of its vulnerability to TS-UF-3 attacks. In this paper, we address this security limitation by presenting an enhanced variant of FROST2, namely, FROST2+ which achieves the TS-SUF-4 security level under the same computational assumptions as the original FROST2. FROST2+ strengthens FROST2 by integrating additional pre-processing token verifications that help mitigate TS-UF-3 and TS-UF-4 vulnerabilities while maintaining practical efficiency. We show that FROST2+ can achieve TS-SUF-4 security not only under the same conditions as the original FROST2 analysis, but also when initialized with a distributed key generation protocol such as PedPoP. Our benchmark using ZCash's FROST library shows that the performance of FROST2+ is comparable to FROST2 and about 64-79% faster than FROST when precomputation is enabled.
tldr: FROST2+ enhances the FROST2 threshold Schnorr signature scheme to achieve TS-SUF-4 security with additional pre-processing token verifications while maintaining practical efficiency.
motivation: FROST2 only achieves TS-SUF-2 security under the one-more discrete logarithm assumption and is vulnerable to TS-UF-3 attacks, which limits its security guarantees for blockchain and distributed systems.
method: The paper integrates additional pre-processing token verifications into FROST2 to mitigate TS-UF-3 and TS-UF-4 vulnerabilities, analyzes security under the same assumptions as FROST2 and with PedPoP distributed key generation, and benchmarks against ZCash's FROST library.
result: FROST2+ achieves TS-SUF-4 security while maintaining performance comparable to FROST2 and about 64-79% faster than FROST when precomputation is enabled.
conclusion: The work provides a practical security enhancement for threshold Schnorr signatures, but it is a classical cryptography paper with no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Response Variability And Stability In Human Reasoning
authors: Clemens Bombach, Rajmadan Lakshmanan, Marco Ragni
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how humans reason -- and how reasoning responses vary across tasks and individuals -- remains a core challenge for modeling and explanation in cognitive science. We investigate the stability of response patterns within reasoners and whether variation in these patterns can be used to predict learning effects. We introduce a formal, geometry-based method to quantify distances between individual reasoning patterns and their internal variability, grounded in heuristic theories. The proposed framework is tested against experimental data via generalized linear mixed-effects models and clustering, where we find that our proposed variation measure interacts with correctness to predict performance gains. Moreover, we find that reasoning patterns are stable over time within the same reasoner. The method is general enough to be applied to other reasoning domains.
tldr: The paper introduces a geometry-based method to quantify variability in individual human reasoning patterns and uses it to predict learning effects and assess pattern stability over time.
motivation: Understanding how humans reason and why responses vary across tasks and individuals remains a core challenge in cognitive science, motivating a formal way to measure intra-individual variability in reasoning.
method: The authors define a geometry-based distance measure between individual reasoning patterns and their internal variability, grounded in heuristic theories, and test it on experimental data using generalized linear mixed-effects models and clustering.
result: The proposed variation measure interacts with correctness to predict performance gains, and reasoning patterns are found to be stable over time within the same reasoner.
conclusion: The framework provides a general, transferable tool for quantifying reasoning stability and predicting learning, applicable to other reasoning domains beyond the one studied.

title: Defense-in-Depth At The Perception-Reasoning Interface Of LLM-Centric Agentic Uav Swarms
authors: Mohammadhossein Homaei, Yousef Emami, Sajad Homayoun, Rahim Taheri, Hao Zhou, Miguel Gutierrez Gaitan, Bo Wei
