This implementation in realistic MAS provides insights that small-scale numerical examples may fail to capture. Results show successful grid stabilization and provision of regulation services from the inverters in the grid using our proposed framework. It can attain up to 78% less overshoot and 30% faster settling time than traditional strategies such as proportional-integral control.
tldr: A data-driven framework for static output-feedback control of linear multi-agent systems, applied to voltage and frequency regulation in electrical networks.
motivation: Traditional control strategies for multi-agent systems often require strong controllability assumptions and online state information, which can be impractical in realistic power grids.
method: The authors develop two algorithms that use offline state and input trajectories to find a Nash equilibrium, then solve a semidefinite program to compute static output-feedback controllers. The framework is tested on nonlinear multi-nodal electrical networks with grid-forming and grid-following inverters.
result: The proposed framework stabilizes the grid and provides regulation services, achieving up to 78% less overshoot and 30% faster settling time compared to proportional-integral control.
conclusion: The data-driven approach enables effective control of multi-agent systems without online information, and validation in high-fidelity nonlinear models demonstrates practical advantages over classical methods.

title: Norm-Additive Maps On The Positive Unit Sphere Of $c^1([0,1])$
authors: Takeshi Miura Kazuki Ezumi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] denote the space of all continuously differentiable real-valued functions on the closed unit interval [MATH]. For [MATH], we equip [MATH] with the norm \[ \Vert_{(p)} := \left(|f(0)|^p+\Vert_{I}^p\right)^{1/p}, & 1\le p<\infty, \\ \max\{|f(0)|,\Vert_{I}\}, & p=\infty, \qquad (f\in C^1(I)), \] where [MATH] denotes the supremum norm on [MATH]. Let [MATH] be the positive unit sphere of [MATH]. A map [MATH] is called norm-additive if \[ \|T(f)+T(g)\|_{(p)}=\|f+g\|_{(p)} \qquad (f,g\in _p^+). \] For [MATH], we prove that every surjective norm-additive map [MATH] is of the form \[ T(f)(t) = f(0)+\int_0^t f'(\tau(s))\,ds \] for all [MATH] and [MATH], where [MATH] is a homeomorphism. Conversely, every map of this form is a surjective norm-additive map. Consequently, every such map extends to a surjective linear isometry from [MATH] onto itself. For [MATH], however, we construct a surjective norm-additive map on [MATH] which is not of the above form and admits no linear extension to [MATH], showing that the assumption [MATH] is essential.
tldr: The authors characterize surjective norm-additive maps on the positive unit sphere of the Banach space C^1([0,1]) equipped with a p-dependent norm, showing such maps are given by composition with a homeomorphism for 1 < p < ∞ and can be pathological for p = 1.
motivation: Norm-additive (or norm-preserving) maps generalize linear isometries and have been studied on various Banach spaces; the paper extends this program to the C^1([0,1]) space with a parametrized norm family.
method: Functional-analytic techniques are used: analyzing the geometric structure of the positive unit sphere, deriving the functional form of surjective norm-additive maps via pointwise evaluation, and constructing a counterexample for p = 1.
result: For 1 < p < ∞ every surjective norm-additive map has the form T(f)(t) = f(0) + ∫_0^t f'(τ(s))ds with τ a homeomorphism and extends to a linear isometry; for p = 1 an explicit surjective norm-additive map is constructed that is not of this form and admits no linear extension.
conclusion: The assumption p > 1 is essential for the rigidity of norm-additive maps in this setting, revealing a sharp boundary between structured and pathological behaviors depending on the norm parameter.

title: Evaluating And Improving The Robustness Of Large Language Models To Input Sequence Variations
authors: Narek Maloyan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in production systems face prompt injections, trojans (backdoors), and manipulation of automatic quality metrics. This thesis develops models, methods, and algorithms for evaluating and improving LLM robustness to adversarial input sequence variations. We propose R_stab(f), a generative robustness metric based on the Jensen-Shannon divergence between per-step output distributions under small input perturbations. For localized attacks we prove V(h) <= 1 - R_class(h), where R_class(h) is the probability that a decision operator h keeps its decision under small perturbations. For non-localized attacks we propose a calibrated empirical model. For LLM-as-a-Judge systems we develop ASA, an adaptive evolutionary black-box attack that reaches an attack success rate (ASR) of up to 73.8%, with transfer between open models up to 62.6%. On Trojan Detection Challenge 2023 data (Pythia-1.4B), surrogate triggers reach REASR ~0.99 while recall of the true triggers is ~0.17 against a baseline of ~0.14. On SaTML CTF 2024 we systematize four classes of bypasses of multi-layer defenses, which reduce the ASR from 90% to 15-25%. Committees of 5-7 heterogeneous models reduce the ASR for Gemma-3-4B by 47-55 percentage points, to 19.3% with 7 models. For agentic systems based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), we propose AttestMCP, which attests tool calls with HMAC-protected packets at under 0.1 ms per call, and the Commit Boundary isolation pattern. On the MCPBench benchmark of 847 scenarios they reduce the average ASR from 53.7% to 12.4%. The methods are implemented in the JudgeGuard and TrojanArmor software suites and the MCPSec module.
tldr: The paper develops metrics, attacks, and defenses for evaluating and improving the robustness of large language models against adversarial input sequence variations, including prompt injection, backdoors, and LLM-as-a-Judge manipulation.
motivation: Large language models deployed in production face adversarial threats such as prompt injections, trojans, and metric manipulation, but systematic evaluation and robustness-improving methods are lacking.
method: The thesis proposes R_stab(f), a generative robustness metric based on Jensen-Shannon divergence; proves a decision-operator bound for localized attacks; develops the ASA evolutionary black-box attack for LLM-as-a-Judge; and introduces AttestMCP with HMAC-protected tool calls and the Commit Boundary isolation pattern for MCP-based agentic systems.
result: ASA reaches up to 73.8% attack success rate with transfer up to 62.6%; on Trojan Detection Challenge data surrogate triggers achieve REASR ~0.99 while true trigger recall is ~0.17; committees of 5-7 heterogeneous models reduce ASR for Gemma-3-4B by 47-55 percentage points to 19.3% with 7 models; AttestMCP reduces average ASR on MCPBench from 53.7% to 12.4%.
conclusion: The proposed methods, implemented in JudgeGuard, TrojanArmor, and MCPSec, improve LLM robustness against input sequence variations and adversarial attacks, with applications to LLM-as-a-Judge and agentic MCP systems.

title: SecJev: Bringing Security Expertise To System One Decision Models
authors: Zheng Chen, Fei Yu, Haohao Huang, Yang Li, Anlong Chen, Lei Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Security workflows need models that turn complex observations and explicit policies into decisions. System One models introduced by Jev return typed predictions and probabilities; security specialization supplies the domain expertise behind those predictions. We introduce SecJev, to our knowledge the first family of Jev-like decision models specialized for security, spanning 0.8B to 9B parameters. Built on Kev's single-pass candidate scorer, SecJev learns Boolean, choice, and ordered decisions from text, telemetry, and observation histories. We develop SecJev-Corpus to unify source-label prediction and explicit-policy evaluation across 14 tasks and eight sources. It covers tool outputs, traffic, federated updates, consensus, authentication, and vehicle messages. Scene-weighted training adapts the models across these domains while preserving a shared typed decision interface. Security specialization improves every model in the family; SecJev-0.8B outperforms general Kev-9B by 20.51 percentage points in task-macro accuracy. Comparisons with answer-only generative fine-tuning show close accuracy and latency with lower peak inference memory. Tests on new source groups reproduce gains over Kev in prompt-injection and traffic decisions, with capture-dependent false alarms. We release adapters, decision heads, SecJev-Corpus, and training and inference code.
tldr: SecJev introduces a family of small (0.8B–9B) security-specialized decision models that learn Boolean, choice, and ordered decisions from text, telemetry, and observation histories, outperforming larger general baselines on security tasks.
motivation: Security workflows require models that convert complex observations and explicit policies into typed decisions with probabilities, but general-purpose decision models lack domain-specific security expertise.
method: The authors build SecJev on a single-pass candidate scorer, train with scene-weighted adaptation across 14 tasks and eight sources unified in the SecJev-Corpus, and compare against answer-only generative fine-tuning.
result: Security specialization improves every model in the family, with SecJev-0.8B beating general Kev-9B by 20.51 percentage points in task-macro accuracy while using lower peak inference memory at comparable latency.
conclusion: Domain-specialized compact decision models offer an efficient path to accurate, low-memory security decision-making, with adapters, corpora, and code publicly released.

title: The Fragility Of Trigger-Tag Mechanisms For Misuse Detection In Open-Weight LLMs
authors: Toluwani Aremu, Manit Baser, Mohan Gurusamy, Nils Lukas, Dinil Mon Divakaran
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-weight language models can be downloaded, modified, and deployed beyond their developers' control, limiting the effectiveness of centrally enforced safeguards. Recent work has therefore proposed mechanisms that produce a detectable signal when a model is used under a target condition, such as generating phishing contents. Although these mechanisms borrow from established techniques, their use for conditional misuse detection in open-weight LLMs is relatively new. Therefore, existing research works have not systematically studied the robustness of trigger-tag mechanisms under adversarial attacks. To close this gap, (i)~we formalize trigger-tags and distinguish , which introduce watermark-inspired signals during decoding, from , which learn backdoor-inspired associations between target conditions and detectable model behavior. Furthermore, (ii)~we introduce \Untag, a unified attack framework that organizes their mechanism-specific attack surfaces into a common taxonomy. We evaluate representative token-level and weight-level trigger-tags using phishing as a case study. We find that while trigger-tags may provide useful evidence in controlled settings, our attacks render the existing trigger-tag mechanisms to be entirely ineffective. Consequently, we argue that these mechanisms should not be treated as robust misuse detectors when attackers can transform outputs or modify open weights.
tldr: The paper formalizes 'trigger-tag' mechanisms for detecting misuse in open-weight LLMs and introduces UNTAG, a unified attack framework that renders existing token-level and weight-level trigger-tags ineffective.
motivation: Open-weight LLMs can be freely modified and redeployed, undermining centrally enforced safeguards, so recent work proposes embedding detectable signals that fire under target misuse conditions such as phishing generation.
method: The authors distinguish watermark-inspired (decoding-time) from backdoor-inspired (learned association) trigger-tags and organize their mechanism-specific attack surfaces into a common taxonomy, which they instantiate as the UNTAG attack framework evaluated with phishing as a case study.
result: Representative token-level and weight-level trigger-tags that appear useful in controlled settings are found to be entirely defeated by the proposed adversarial attacks, making them ineffective as misuse detectors.
conclusion: The authors argue trigger-tag mechanisms should not be treated as robust misuse detectors whenever attackers can transform outputs or modify open weights.

title: EvoRiskBench: An Evolving Benchmark For Runtime Security Risks In Workspace Agents
authors: Shiyi Kuang, Xuemei Luo, Kun Liu, Junhai Li, Rui Tian, Feng Shi, Bo Shen, Nianyu Li, Dehui Li, Ping Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Workspace agents combine large language models with execution harnesses to perform stateful, multi-step tasks that access or modify external resources. Existing benchmarks leave gaps in executable coverage of their runtime security risks, while evolving model capabilities, harnesses, tools, and threats motivate benchmark evolution. We introduce EvoRiskBench, an evolving benchmark organized around the EP-Path-EF framework, which links an initial risk entry point to a one-hop technical effect through an agent-mediated risk path. The framework defines nine entry-point categories and five effect categories; a 20-participant study supports their interpretability and classification consistency on representative cases. Guided by this framework, an automated end-to-end workflow constructs and executes risk cases in isolated environments and independently verifies outcomes using runtime traces and environment states. The benchmark provides a reproducible dataset of 450 adversarial tasks across six scenarios. We evaluate nine model-harness configurations spanning three models (GPT-5.6 Sol, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, and Claude Opus 5) and three harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw). Our results reveal substantial vulnerabilities across systems. The most vulnerable configuration, Codex with DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, reaches a 68.44% attack success rate (ASR), indicating that configuration of workspace agent is insufficient to ensure secure autonomous execution. ASR varies more across models than harnesses, and harness differences depend on the model. The benchmark cases and evaluation platform will be released after completion of artifact safety and reproducibility checks.
tldr: EvoRiskBench is an evolving benchmark for evaluating runtime security risks in LLM-based workspace agents using the EP-Path-EF risk framework.
motivation: Workspace agents that couple large language models with execution harnesses can access and modify external resources, yet existing benchmarks insufficiently cover their executable runtime security risks.
method: The authors define an EP-Path-EF framework with nine entry-point and five effect categories, validated by a 20-participant study, and build an automated end-to-end workflow that constructs and executes 450 adversarial tasks across six scenarios in isolated environments with independent outcome verification.
result: Evaluating nine model-harness configurations (GPT-5.6 Sol, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, Claude Opus 5 across Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw), the most vulnerable configuration reached a 68.44% attack success rate, with ASR varying more across models than harnesses.
conclusion: The findings show that current workspace agent configurations remain substantially vulnerable, indicating that harness configuration alone is insufficient to guarantee secure autonomous execution.

title: Human Mobility Shapes How Urban Policy Effects Spread Across Cities
authors: Bijin Joseph, Hamish Gibbs, Takahiro Yabe, Esteban Moro
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Urban policies are often evaluated assuming their effects decay with geographic distance. However, cities are systems of human movement, and policy effects propagate through individual mobility rather than spatial proximity alone. This study demonstrates that neglecting mobility can systematically distort estimates of how urban policies affect activity. Using large-scale mobility data, we estimate the causal effects of three transportation interventions in Boston and New York City using both conventional geographic and mobility-based definitions of exposure. Geographic designs detect no effects, or even negative ones. When exposure is defined through mobility networks, the same interventions reveal substantial behavioral change. Boston's free-fare program increases overall activity by approximately 16%, with more pronounced effects among lower-income communities. Open Streets programs significantly increase visits to nearby businesses, particularly food establishments. For congestion pricing, geographic approaches suggest a decline in activity in Manhattan, while a mobility-based perspective indicates no net reduction but a shift away from shopping and grocery destinations. Analysis across 138 metropolitan areas in eight countries further reveals that geographic and mobility-network distances diverge locally in every city, indicating that this discrepancy is a general characteristic of urban mobility. Collectively, these findings show that urban policies operate not only where they are implemented but where and how people move, so their impact must be measured through mobility rather than through space.
tldr: Urban policy effects propagate through human mobility networks rather than geographic proximity, and ignoring this systematically distorts causal estimates of policy impact.
motivation: Urban policies are conventionally evaluated assuming effects decay with geographic distance, but cities are systems of human movement, so spatial-proximity designs may misestimate true policy effects.
method: Using large-scale mobility data, the authors estimate causal effects of three transportation interventions in Boston and NYC under both conventional geographic and mobility-network definitions of exposure, then extend the distance comparison to 138 metropolitan areas across eight countries.
result: Geographic designs detect null or negative effects, while mobility-based exposure reveals substantial behavioral change (~16% activity increase for Boston's free-fare program, more visits to nearby businesses under Open Streets, and a destination shift rather than net decline under congestion pricing); geographic and mobility distances diverge in every city studied.
conclusion: Urban policy impact should be measured through mobility networks rather than space, since policies operate where and how people move, not merely where they are implemented.

title: A Theory Of Nested Cascading In Directed Logic
authors: Ihar Babushkin, Oliver Melchert, Ayhan Demircan, Uwe Morgner
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In directed logic (DL), electronically controlled optical elements serve as photonic gates. Such electro-optical elements are of mixed nature: they have two inputs--electronic and optical--but only one, optical, output. This makes cascading such gates without repeated conversion between optical and electronic representations cumbersome. This problem can be largely overcome using the nested cascading scheme proposed by Shamir and Hardy [Opt. Express, 17, 150 (2007)]. Although promising as a solution to the cascading problem, the Shamir-Hardy scheme has so far been proved or implemented only for a few simplest cases. Here, we develop a general rigorous theory of nested cascading, valid for an arbitrary number of gates. We propose a variant of the algorithm which easily extendable to large number of gates, and rigorously prove its validity. Furthermore, we analyze how nested cascading scales with the size of the corresponding Boolean formula. We show that good (linear) scalability is guaranteed in many important cases, while the average scaling with respect to the corresponding Boolean formulas is only moderately polynomial, with an exponent of approximately 3/2. Yet, the worst-case scaling remains exponential with respect to more general Boolean circuits allowing sharing and reuse of intermediate results.
tldr: The paper develops a general theory of nested cascading for directed logic photonic gates, proving scalability properties for Boolean formula implementations.
motivation: Directed logic uses electro-optical gates with mixed electronic and optical inputs, making cascading without repeated conversions difficult; the Shamir-Hardy nested cascading scheme was only previously proved for simple cases.
method: The authors formulate a rigorous general theory of nested cascading valid for arbitrary gate numbers, propose an extendable algorithm, and analyze its scaling with respect to Boolean formula size.
result: They prove the algorithm's validity, show linear scalability in many important cases, and find average polynomial scaling with exponent about 3/2, while worst-case scaling remains exponential for general Boolean circuits with sharing and reuse.
conclusion: The theory provides a foundation for nested cascading in directed logic, enabling efficient implementation for many Boolean formulas but highlighting fundamental limitations for arbitrary circuits.

title: Joint Movement And Compression Ratio Design For Mobile Embodied Ai Networks (mean)
authors: Yahao Ding, Jiaxiang Wang, Zhouxiang Zhao, Zhaohui Yang, Mingzhe Chen, Mohammad Shikh-Bahaei
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mobile embodied AI networks (MEAN) enable embodied agents to perceive, reason, communicate, and act in wireless environments. In such networks, agent mobility can improve channel conditions, while semantic compression can reduce transmission payloads. However, movement consumes energy, and stronger compression incurs additional computational cost. This paper studies joint movement, semantic compression, and transmit power design for an uplink MEAN system. We formulate a max-min energy efficiency (EE) problem by jointly optimizing transmit power, movement distance, and semantic compression ratio under controllable power constraints. The problem is non-convex due to the coupled signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), mobility-dependent channel gains, and fractional EE objective. To solve it, we propose an alternating optimization (AO)-Dinkelbach algorithm, where the fractional objective is handled by the Dinkelbach transformation, transmit power is updated via successive convex approximation (SCA), and movement distance is updated by coordinate-wise grid search. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme outperforms no-mobility and no-compression baselines, demonstrating the benefit of jointly exploiting mobility control, semantic compression, and power allocation in MEAN.
tldr: This paper jointly optimizes movement, semantic compression ratio, and transmit power for mobile embodied AI networks to maximize minimum energy efficiency.
motivation: Mobile embodied AI networks can benefit from agent mobility to improve channels and semantic compression to reduce payloads, but movement costs energy and stronger compression increases computation cost.
method: The authors formulate a non-convex max-min energy efficiency problem and solve it with an alternating optimization and Dinkelbach algorithm, using successive convex approximation for power and coordinate-wise grid search for movement distance.
result: Simulations show the proposed joint design outperforms no-mobility and no-compression baselines.
conclusion: Jointly exploiting mobility control, semantic compression, and power allocation improves energy efficiency in mobile embodied AI networks.

title: Structure-Driven Methodology: An Emerging Cross-Domain Paradigm
authors: Shengchang Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article proposes and articulates structure-driven methodology as an emerging cross-domain paradigm. In contrast to the objective-driven paradigm that has dominated inverse-problem solving for over two centuries, structure-driven methodology advocates identifying and exploiting the intrinsic structure of a problem to construct the solution method directly, rather than approaching the solution through iterative search. Drawing on examples from the Liouville-variant Goldbach conjecture, the three-dimensional Kakeya conjecture, Noether's theorem, and the author's nearly four decades of geophysical inversion practice, the article illustrates the common logic of structure-driven thinking in number theory, pure mathematics, physics, and seismic imaging. The author also systematically proposes the Structure-Driven Inversion (SDI) paradigm, comprising Mathematical Structure-Driven Inversion (MSDI) and Physical Structure-Driven Inversion (PSDI). Structure-driven methodology does not negate objective-driven methodology but complements it: objective-driven is a general search strategy, whereas structure-driven is a custom direct strategy. The article concludes that the significance of this shift lies not only in efficiency gains but also in cognitive deepening---when facing complex problems, the first question is no longer ``how to solve the problem faster'' but ``what is the structure of the problem.''.
tldr: The paper proposes structure-driven methodology as a cross-domain paradigm for solving problems by directly exploiting intrinsic structure rather than iterative objective-driven search.
motivation: The author aims to articulate a general problem-solving philosophy that contrasts with and complements the dominant objective-driven paradigm, drawing on examples from number theory, pure mathematics, physics, and geophysical inversion.
method: The article synthesizes case studies of structure-driven thinking, including the Liouville-variant Goldbach conjecture, the three-dimensional Kakeya conjecture, Noether's theorem, and the author's four decades of geophysical inversion experience, and formalizes it as Structure-Driven Inversion (SDI) with mathematical and physical variants.
result: The paper argues that structure-driven methodology yields both efficiency gains and cognitive deepening, positioning objective-driven approaches as general search strategies and structure-driven approaches as custom direct strategies.
conclusion: The significance of this shift lies in reframing the first question from 'how to solve the problem faster' to 'what is the structure of the problem,' suggesting a broad cross-domain paradigm for complex problem solving.

title: An Adaptive Symplectic Proximal Point Algorithm: Faster Convergence And Improved Numerical Performance
authors: Yi Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The proximal point algorithm (PPA) stands as a fundamental approach for solving monotone inclusion problems. Notably, several key convex optimization algorithms have been proven to be specific instances of PPA. Given the importance of the PPA, there has been growing interest in developing its accelerated variants. However, for some specific cases, the PPA converges faster than the accelerated PPAs. In this paper, we mainly study an adaptive version of symplectic accelerated PPA, called adaptive symplectic proximal point algorithm (ASPPA). We first prove that the convergence rate of ASPPA with respect to the square norm term is [MATH], which is the same as the convergence rate of some accelerated PPAs. Also, we show that ASPPA exists exponential convergence rate when solving strongly monotone inclusion problem. Our numerical experiments indicate that the performance of ASPPA is very good.
tldr: The paper proposes an adaptive symplectic proximal point algorithm (ASPPA) for monotone inclusion problems and analyzes its convergence properties.
motivation: The proximal point algorithm is fundamental for monotone inclusions and has accelerated variants, but in some cases standard PPA converges faster, motivating adaptive symplectic acceleration.
method: The authors develop an adaptive version of the symplectic accelerated proximal point algorithm and prove convergence rates for the square norm term and exponential convergence for strongly monotone inclusion problems.
result: ASPPA achieves the same convergence rate as some accelerated PPAs and exhibits exponential convergence for strongly monotone problems, with numerical experiments showing strong performance.
conclusion: ASPPA provides a competitive adaptive optimization method, though the work is purely mathematical optimization and not connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Containing The Autonomous Operator: A Defense-in-Depth Framework And Reference Architecture For Securing Ai Agents On Kubernetes
authors: Simhadri Podala Narasimha
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are moving from chat interfaces into infrastructure operations, where they read telemetry, call tools, generate and execute code, and change the state of production Kubernetes clusters. This collapses a boundary that conventional cloud-native security assumes: the boundary between data and control. Content that an agent merely reads (a log line, a ticket, a tool description) can redirect what it does. This paper argues that the model must not be treated as a security boundary and that agent safety on Kubernetes is therefore an infrastructure problem: every guarantee must continue to hold under the assumption that the agent is fully compromised by prompt injection. We contribute (i) a threat model and ten-class threat taxonomy for agents operating on and within Kubernetes, aligned with emerging OWASP guidance for agentic applications; (ii) nine design principles, centered on complete mediation at the tool boundary and on breaking the combination of untrusted input, sensitive access, and external egress; (iii) a seven-layer defense-in-depth framework that maps each principle to native or widely adopted Kubernetes mechanisms: workload identity, RBAC and ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, gVisor/Kata sandboxing via the SIG Apps Agent Sandbox project, FQDN-aware egress policy, an agent/MCP gateway with policy-as-code over tool arguments, and eBPF runtime enforcement; (iv) a reference architecture with concrete policy artifacts and per-layer bindings for Amazon EKS, Azure Kubernetes Service, and Google Kubernetes Engine; and (v) a qualitative evaluation comprising a threat-control coverage matrix and four attack walkthroughs, with a proposed empirical methodology. We report no measured attack-success or overhead figures; instead we identify residual risks and the measurements needed to validate the framework.
tldr: This paper proposes a defense-in-depth framework and reference architecture for securing LLM-based autonomous agents operating on Kubernetes clusters, treating the agent as fully compromised and enforcing security at the infrastructure layer.
motivation: LLM agents are increasingly used for infrastructure operations, blurring the data/control boundary and introducing prompt-injection risks that conventional cloud-native security models do not address.
method: The authors develop a threat model and ten-class taxonomy, nine design principles, a seven-layer defense-in-depth framework mapped to Kubernetes mechanisms (workload identity, RBAC, sandboxing, egress policy, gateways, eBPF), and a reference architecture with policy artifacts for EKS, AKS, and GKE.
result: They provide a qualitative evaluation via a threat-control coverage matrix and attack walkthroughs, but report no measured attack-success or overhead figures; residual risks and needed measurements are identified.
conclusion: The paper argues that agent safety on Kubernetes must be treated as an infrastructure problem, and offers a structured framework and architecture, while noting that empirical validation remains future work.

title: A Mechanistic Model Of The Human Menstrual Cycle
authors: Lena Reitinger, Nina Nikic, Esma Hamzic-Jahic, Barbara Arbeithuber, Andreas Springer, Werner Haselmayr, Stefan Angerbauer
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The human menstrual cycle is regulated by complex hormonal feedback mechanisms which are essential for reproductive health. Existing mathematical models either rely on simplified phenomenological assumptions or achieve physiological accuracy at the cost of high mathematical complexity and computational costs. This paper presents a novel mechanistic model which balances biological realism with mathematical simplicity. The proposed framework describes the dynamics of the four central cycle-driving hormones, namely follicle stimulating hormone, luteinizing hormone, estradiol, and progesterone, using a system of ordinary differential equations. Mechanistic detail is incorporated through representations of feedback mechanisms, follicular development, luteinization, vascularization of the corpus luteum, and aspects of hormone synthesis mechanisms. Despite its comparatively low complexity, the model reproduces characteristic trends of hormone activity and concentration dynamics reported in experimental data. Due to its computational efficiency and modularity, the model is well suited as a basis for extended in-silico experiments, including applications in pharmacology and personalized medicine. Our results demonstrate that targeted incorporation of biological mechanisms enables accurate yet tractable modeling of endocrine system dynamics.
tldr: A mechanistic ordinary differential equation model of the human menstrual cycle that balances biological realism with low mathematical complexity.
motivation: Existing mathematical models of the menstrual cycle either oversimplify physiology or are computationally expensive and mathematically complex, limiting their use in in-silico experiments.
method: The authors construct a system of ordinary differential equations for four key hormones (FSH, LH, estradiol, progesterone), incorporating feedback mechanisms, follicular development, luteinization, vascularization of the corpus luteum, and hormone synthesis.
result: The model reproduces characteristic trends of hormone activity and concentration dynamics observed in experimental data despite its comparatively low complexity.
conclusion: The framework is computationally efficient and modular, making it suitable for extended in-silico experiments in pharmacology and personalized medicine.

title: Reversing The Clock: Layout-Aware Recovery Of Design Intent From Clock Distribution Networks
authors: Sascha Tommasone, Zehra Karada\u{g}, Christopher Pawlowicz, Michael Green, Bruno Machado Trindade, Eunsung Seo, Christof Paar, Ren\'e Walendy, Steffen Becker
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hardware reverse engineering supports competitive analysis and hardware assurance by recovering information about an integrated circuit (IC) from its physical implementation. While existing techniques primarily recover the gate-level netlist, which represents logical functionality, they often overlook physical design decisions such as placement, routing, delay insertion, and interconnect optimization. The clock distribution network encapsulates many of these decisions; however, no prior published work has recovered this network from a fabricated IC to infer design intent. We present a layout-aware methodology that recovers and analyzes the clock distribution network by integrating a recovered gate-level netlist with layout information extracted from scanning electron microscope imagery. Our four-phase pipeline recovers clock-tree topology, buffering, gating and switching, interconnect delay, and crosstalk-mitigation measures. We demonstrate our methodology on a commercial 450 nm IC, recovering a global H-tree backbone with local X-tree-like branching, identifying an independent clock tree and global clock gating, quantifying latency, skew, and routing lengths, and confirming the absence of dedicated crosstalk mitigation. Together, these findings let us reason about the designer's intent. To encourage further research and support reproducibility, we release our clock tree recovery algorithm as open source.
tldr: A layout-aware methodology recovers clock distribution network design intent from fabricated ICs using SEM imagery and a recovered gate-level netlist.
motivation: Hardware reverse engineering typically recovers only gate-level netlists and overlooks physical design decisions such as clock distribution, which encode designer intent.
method: The four-phase pipeline integrates a recovered gate-level netlist with layout information from scanning electron microscope imagery to recover clock-tree topology, buffering, gating, interconnect delay, and crosstalk mitigation.
result: Demonstrated on a commercial 450 nm IC, it recovered a global H-tree backbone, local X-tree branching, independent clock tree, global clock gating, and quantified latency, skew, and routing lengths.
conclusion: The approach enables reasoning about designer intent from clock distribution networks and releases the recovery algorithm as open source, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Asymptotic Analysis Of Trading Fees In Cfmm
authors: Peiyang Jin, Clouds, Jing Qian
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As the dominant trading mechanism in decentralized finance, Automated Market Maker has been widely studied in research. However, limited research has been done with the trading fees taken into consideration. In this work, we study how much trading fee Liquidity Providers(LPs) can receive from arbitrage trading when the fee rate approaches zero. We give a closed-form formula for it and our result shows that the trading fees generated by arbitrage trading can fully offset the LVR loss when the price process is continuous. We further extend our conclusions to price processes with jumps and the theoretical analysis shows that jumps are the only cause of LP loss apart from market risks. Our results provide practical guidance for AMM designers as well as LPs.
tldr: This paper asymptotically analyzes trading fees in constant function market makers, showing that arbitrage-generated fees offset LVR losses for continuous prices, while jumps are the only additional source of LP loss.
motivation: Automated market makers dominate decentralized finance, but prior research has largely ignored trading fees, leaving unclear how much fee revenue liquidity providers can earn from arbitrage.
method: The authors derive a closed-form formula for trading fees received by LPs as the fee rate approaches zero, then extend the analysis to price processes with jumps.
result: For continuous price processes, arbitrage trading fees fully offset LVR loss; for jump processes, jumps are the only cause of LP loss apart from market risk.
conclusion: The results offer practical guidance for AMM designers and liquidity providers regarding fee structures and loss mitigation.

title: Two-qutrit Werner State Is Always Local
authors: Muhammad Mohsin Pawe\l{} Caban
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In our paper, we show that a two-qutrit Werner state admits a local hidden-variable model for all values of the parameter in a scenario involving two projective measurements per site, with three outcomes per measurement. To this end, we derive a simple sufficient condition under which a two-qutrit state satisfies the Collins-Gisin-Linden-Massar-Popescu inequality for arbitrary choices of Alice's and Bob's observables, and show that the Werner state always satisfies this condition. Next, we use the fact that any two-qutrit state satisfying the Collins-Gisin-Linden-Massar-Popescu inequality for arbitrary choices of Alice's and Bob's observables admits a local hidden variable model.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Spatial Functional $k$-Nearest-Neighbour Regression Under Polynomial Dependence
authors: St\'ephane Bouka
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates non-parametric regression estimation when the explanatory variable takes values in a separable Hilbert space and observations are sampled over an increasing regular spatial lattice. Under a rigorous field-to-field independence setup between covariates and errors, we explore the structural and asymptotic concentration properties of the functional [MATH]-nearest-neighbour ([MATH]-NN) estimator. By establishing a sharp pathwise deterministic sandwiching framework for the data-driven random bandwidth, we successfully decouple the local infinite-dimensional small-ball profile from the polynomial covariance decay of the neighborhood indicators. Pointwise convergence rates are derived across short-range, critical, and long-range spatial regimes, revealing a combined penalty term that reflects both covariate spatial interaction and response error memory. Furthermore, uniform consistency over compact subsets is established for unbounded sub-Gaussian error processes through metric entropy and indicator boundary shell chaining. Structured polynomial simulations confirm our theoretical rates and exemplify the precise mechanics of the spatial long-range bottleneck.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: An Applicative Multiset Path Order (Extended Version)
authors: Nao Hirokawa, Teppei Saito, Teppei Tanaka, Wataru Yachi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.02973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a variant of the multiset path order for untyped applicative term rewriting. Compared to existing work, our variant incorporates two distinctive features, dubbed arity assignment and reification, to overcome difficulties in handling partial and variable application.
tldr: The paper introduces an applicative multiset path order for untyped applicative term rewriting, using arity assignment and reification to handle partial and variable application.
motivation: Existing multiset path orders have difficulty dealing with untyped applicative terms where function symbols may be partially applied or applied to variable arguments.
method: The authors define a variant of the multiset path order with two features, arity assignment and reification, to adapt the ordering to untyped applicative term rewriting systems.
result: The proposed order overcomes the limitations of previous approaches for partial and variable application in this setting.
conclusion: This work extends termination ordering techniques for applicative term rewriting, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Passing The Test You Trained On: Re-evaluating Prompt-Injection Detectors For Llm Agents
authors: Zhuowen Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.03448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents increasingly screen tool outputs with small prompt-injection detectors, and teams choose among detectors by their scores on public benchmarks. We ask whether those scores predict how a detector behaves inside an agent. We replay the ground-truth tool calls of two agent benchmarks, AgentDojo and tau-bench, without an LLM to obtain tool outputs that are benign by construction, label injected outputs by differential replay, and evaluate fifteen detectors, including Meta's Prompt Guard 2, and two task-aware LLM judges on these outputs and on the BIPIA benchmark. Detection rankings transfer poorly between benchmarks: the best detector on BIPIA catches 2% of AgentDojo injections at a 1% false-positive rate, and a detector that catches 72% of AgentDojo injections catches 15% on tau-bench. False-positive rates on tool outputs, which range from none to over 90%, do transfer between the two agent benchmarks. Where training data is public, the form of the training inputs explains the results. The BIPIA leader was trained on full BIPIA inputs, but having seen InjecAgent's attack strings as short prompts does not help it find them inside tool outputs; the best detector on both agent benchmarks shares no data with any benchmark and was trained on agent-style inputs. Evaluations meant to inform deployment should use the agent's own tool outputs, report detection at a low false-positive rate, and audit what the detector was trained on.
tldr: The paper re-evaluates prompt-injection detectors for LLM agents and finds that public benchmark scores transfer poorly to real agent tool outputs.
motivation: Teams choose prompt-injection detectors based on public benchmark scores, but it is unclear whether those scores predict how detectors behave inside deployed LLM agents.
method: The authors replay ground-truth tool calls from AgentDojo and tau-bench without an LLM to obtain benign outputs, label injected outputs by differential replay, and evaluate fifteen detectors plus two task-aware LLM judges on these outputs and on BIPIA.
result: Detection rankings transfer poorly between benchmarks, with the best BIPIA detector catching only 2% of AgentDojo injections at a 1% false-positive rate, while false-positive rates on tool outputs do transfer and training input form explains detector performance.
conclusion: Evaluations meant to inform deployment should use the agent's own tool outputs, report detection at a low false-positive rate, and audit what the detector was trained on.
